source_text: Aetas igitur illa sicut misericordiam Christi praedicat innovata, id est, innovantis mysterii virtute provecta; ita iniquitatem iudicis, infamiam iustitiae, aut accusata, aut aggravata convincit.
pass_a_gloss: That age therefore, as when renewed it preaches the mercy of Christ, that is, advanced by the virtue of the renewing mystery; so, either accused or aggravated, it convicts the iniquity of the judge, the infamy of justice.
pass_b_english: Thus infancy, when renewed, that is, advanced by the power of the renewing mystery, proclaims Christ's mercy. But when infancy is accused or burdened with guilt, it exposes the judge's injustice and the disgrace of his justice.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
